The minimum value of \((x+4)^2+4\) is 4.\par So \((x+4)^2+4\ge4\).\par Therefore, \(x^2+8x+20\ge4\).

\(kx^2+5kx+3=0\) has no real roots, so \(b^2-4ac<0\).\[\begin{aligned}(5k)^2-4k(3)&<0\\25k^2-12k&<0\\k(25k-12)&<0\\0<k&<\tfrac{12}{25}\end{aligned}\]When \(k=0\):\[(0)x^2+5(0)x+3=0,\qquad3=0\]which is impossible, so no real roots.\par So combining these:\[0\le k<\tfrac{12}{25}\]

18 A circle has equation \((x-1)^2+y^2=k\), where \(k>0\).\par The straight line \(L\) with equation \(y=ax\) cuts the circle at two distinct points.\par Prove that \(k>\dfrac{a^2}{1+a^2}\).

Substituting \(y=ax\) into \((x-1)^2+y^2=k\):\[\begin{aligned}(x-1)^2+a^2x^2&=k\\x^2-2x+1+a^2x^2-k&=0\\x^2(1+a^2)-2x+1-k&=0\end{aligned}\]The straight line cuts the circle at two distinct points, so this equation has two distinct real roots, so\[\begin{aligned}b^2-4ac&>0\\(-2)^2-4(1+a^2)(1-k)&>0\\4-4(1-k+a^2-ka^2)&>0\\4k-4a^2+4ka^2&>0\\-a^2+k+ka^2&>0\\-a^2+k(1+a^2)&>0\\k&>\frac{a^2}{1+a^2}\end{aligned}\]

blocks.tex: 4 Prove that all cube numbers are either a multiple of 9 or 1 more or 1 less than a multiple of 9.
7 Prove that for all real values of \(x\)\[(x+6)^2\ge2x+11\]

Break down the integers into numbers divisible by 3 and numbers giving a remainder of 1 or 2 when divided by 3.\[(3n)^3=27n^3=9n(3n^2)\]which is a multiple of 9.\[\begin{aligned}(3n+1)^3&=27n^3+27n^2+9n+1\\&=9n(3n^2+3n+1)+1\end{aligned}\]which is one more than a multiple of 9.

\[\begin{aligned}(3n+2)^3&=27n^3+54n^2+36n+8\\&=9n(3n^2+6n+4)+8\end{aligned}\]which is one less than a multiple of 9.\par So all cube numbers are either a multiple of 9 or 1 more or 1 less than a multiple of 9.

9 a Prove that for any positive numbers \(p\) and \(q\):\[p+q>\sqrt{4pq}\]\par b Show, by means of a counter-example, that this inequality does not hold when \(p\) and \(q\) are both negative. \hfill\(\text{(2 m}\ldots\)
8 Given that \(a\) is a positive real number, prove that:\[a+\frac1a\ge2\]

As \(a\) is positive, multiplying both sides by \(a\) does not reverse the inequality.\par So \(a^2+1\ge2a\).\par Then \(a^2-2a+1\ge0\).\par Factorising gives\par \((a-1)^2\ge0\) which we know is true.

\textbf{a} By squaring both sides, consider \((p+q)^2\).\[\begin{aligned}(p+q)^2&=p^2+2pq+q^2\\&=(p-q)^2+4pq\end{aligned}\]\((p-q)^2\ge0\) since it is a square, so \((p+q)^2\ge4pq\).\par \(p\) and \(q\) are both positive, so \(p>0\) and \(q>0\). Therefore, \(p+q>0\).\par So \(p+q\ge\sqrt{4pq}\).
\textbf{b} When \(p=q=-1,p+q=-2\) and \(\sqrt{4pq}=2\), but \(-2<2\), i.e. \(p+q<\sqrt{4pq}\) which is inconsistent.
